---
title: "How do I calculate the standard error of a sample mean?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I calculate the standard error of a sample mean?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Count the usable observations.

2. Calculate their sample standard deviation.

3. Divide sd by sqrt(n) and label it as an estimated standard error.

## Runnable example

```{r}
x <- c(11,12,14,16,17,18,19,21)
n <- length(x)
se <- sd(x)/sqrt(n)
print(c(n=n,mean=mean(x),sample_sd=sd(x),SE=se))
```

## Interpret the result

Standard error is smaller than the sample standard deviation because it measures uncertainty in the sample mean, not the dispersion of the measurements.

## Check before using real data

Standard error is not the spread of individual observations. Independence and sampling design matter.
